triage.note: PR #61 R15 / TD-160, and it is a rejection re-argued rather than a debt row re-stated. TD-160 rejected deriving `DEPLOY_EXCLUDED` from the trigger because it 'means a full `extract_items` sweep of 44 filings at process start (seconds of CPU, and a hard dependency on the extractor from the LISTING path, which today is pure stdlib directory reading)'. Every word of that is true of an IMPORT-time derivation in the web layer, and R15's point is that an EVAL-time derivation was never costed: measured at 4.6s against a 44s `fast` suite, with no new import on any request path. So the sweep runs here. The deployment still reads a frozenset — the listing path stays pure stdlib — and this case is what keeps that frozenset honest. Equality in BOTH directions: a fixture that fires and is not excluded is R1's hole re-opening with nobody having edited anything, and a fixture excluded that does not fire is a demo entry withheld for no reason, which nothing else would catch. Re-derived here rather than cited: `low_item_coverage` fires 2/44 -> ['intc-2025', 'xref-index-collapse'].
triage.note_negative_space: FAST SUITE ONLY, deliberately. The PostToolUse hook runs `invariant` on every edit and 4.6s per edit-batch is a real tax; the pre-commit gate runs `fast`, so the property is enforced at every commit, which is the last moment a hand-maintained set can drift. It does not derive the set AT RUNTIME — `DEPLOY_EXCLUDED` is still what the deployment reads, and a tree edited and deployed without running the gate would still ship a stale set. And since TD-158's door, the exclusion is no longer what makes the spend bounded: it is the second layer, and this case keeps that layer from rotting rather than being the brake.
